title: Jira Cloud: Make Work Ready to Act On
headline:
Turn a vague ask
into ready work.
need: An ambiguous work item moves to Done without evidence that the requested result was delivered.
outcomes: Choose a work-item description with observable acceptance criteria.
Select a status action consistent with a fictional team workflow.

concepts.title: Capture an actionable work item
concepts.body: Current Jira Cloud documentation uses work item; some sites and teams still say issue. Create opens a form whose fields depend on the space, work type and configuration. This lesson uses a simplified simulation, not a pixel-exact tenant tutorial.

concepts.title: Write the result and acceptance criteria
concepts.body: A useful description names the outcome and how the team will check it. Acceptance criteria are an observable agreement, not merely a due date. The format used here is a training example, not a mandatory Jira field or universal team policy.

concepts.title: Use the team workflow
concepts.body: Statuses represent stages of work; transitions move between them. Available transitions depend on workflow rules and permissions. In this fictional team, work moves To do → In progress → Review → Done after evidence review.

concepts.title: Keep the record useful
concepts.body: Record the blocker, evidence or next action that another teammate needs. Do not move an item to Done simply because effort was spent. Check the team’s completion criteria and avoid putting sensitive customer information into a public example.

example.title: A training-job-aid request
example.body: Weak request: “Update training.” Improved request: “Publish the revised escalation job aid for new trainers.” The fictional criteria are: accurate three-step procedure, accessible headings, and reviewer confirmation.
steps: Select the correct work context and type for your tenant.
Describe the outcome and three observable checks.
Work on the job aid and attach or link approved evidence.
Move to Review while confirmation is pending; use Done only after this team’s criteria are met.

practice.prompt: The job aid is drafted but reviewer confirmation is missing. In this fictional workflow, what fits?
options: Done because the author finished writing
Review, with the evidence and outstanding check recorded
practice.feedback: The team’s agreement requires review before Done; the status should represent the real state.

draft.prompt: Draft a work item for updating a trainer checklist. Include the outcome, two acceptance criteria and the next status when review is still pending.
draft.label: Your work-item brief
draft.model: Update the trainer checklist for the revised handoff. Criteria: all four handoff steps match the approved process; a reviewer confirms the accessible version. Status: Review while confirmation is pending.
criteria: States a useful next action or reviewer need

options: Publish the revised trainer escalation job aid
quiz.feedback: The title identifies the intended deliverable.

quiz.prompt: Which is an observable acceptance criterion?
options: All three approved escalation steps appear in order
quiz.feedback: A reviewer can inspect the deliverable against this condition.

quiz.prompt: What can change the fields in the Create form?
quiz.feedback: Configured work types and contexts affect the form.

quiz.prompt: Review is required and not yet complete. Which state fits this sample?
quiz.feedback: The state reflects the unmet review condition.

quiz.prompt: A needed transition is unavailable. What is a useful next step?
options: Check workflow rules and permissions with the appropriate owner
quiz.feedback: Available transitions are controlled by the configured workflow.

jobaid: Move status when the team’s conditions are met.

transcript:
Time: 3 minutes. You support the fictional Harbor app. A colleague reports: ‘The export is broken.’ Your task is to produce work that a developer and tester can act on without guessing. Ask for the affected action, environment, expected result, observed result, frequency, and impact. Use synthetic examples only.

Evidence packet: in Harbor demo build 2.4, select the October orders, choose CSV export, and open the file. The screen lists 12 rows but the export contains 10. It happens on two attempts with the same sample dataset. Search the correct Jira space for export, CSV, missing rows, and similar reports; clear unintended filters if results look incomplete. Available search views vary by tenant.

Worked duplicate review: HBR-71 concerns a PDF layout problem. HBR-84 describes a CSV export omitting the last two rows in demo build 2.4. HBR-84 is a strong match; inspect its context and status before creating another record. If it represents the same defect, add relevant new evidence through your team’s process. Similar wording alone does not prove identical cause.

Current Atlassian Cloud documentation uses work item and space; older interfaces may say issue and project.
